This command adds a new domain to the your Data Governance Edition deployment.
The Data Governance Server constructs an in-memory map of the Active Directory forest and domain structure where it is deployed. Administrators responsible for the Data Governance Edition deployment must register Service Accounts with the system and link them with domains. The link between a Service Account and an Active Directory domain makes it a “Managed Domain”.
Note: Only domains that have been previously synchronized into the One Identity Manager database are available to be managed by Data Governance Edition.

This command adds a managed host to your deployment. A managed host is any network object that can host resources and can be assigned an agent to monitor security and resource activity. Currently supported hosts include Windows computers, Windows clusters, NetApp Attached Storage Devices, EMC Storage Devices, and SharePoint farms.
You can also add generic managed hosts (computers other than those on the supported list) to remotely scan their resources.
Once you have added a managed host, you can begin to manage the data contained within it.

Enables the resource activity tracking.
Resource activity tracking is available for locally managed Windows servers, SharePoint farms, and supported NetApp and EMC remotely managed hosts. It is used to collect data on identities, reads, writes, creates, deletes, renames and security changes on securable objects. This information is required for several report types, including the Resource Activity report.

maml:description.maml:para: Registers an account as a service account for Data Governance Edition.

This command registers an account as a data governance service account.
Data Governance Edition consolidates security information across many domains and forests by accessing these network entities using stored credentials (Service Accounts). These Service Accounts are Active Directory users granted the appropriate permissions in their respective domains and registered with Data Governance Edition.
The service account performs actions that a local service cannot. For example, a remotely scanning agent needs a service account to access the files on the managed host it's scanning.
Note: Service Accounts must have administrative privileges in the domains they are registered with. This allows the Data Governance Server to elevate its identity to these accounts and perform actions such as agent deployments and Active Directory queries.

maml:description.maml:para: Retrieves the activity associated with a resource.

This command provides a granular list of activities recorded over a period of time that you can use to verify proper resource usage and make decisions on modifying access.
When running the command, you can specify multiple resources to report on and narrow the scope by providing exclusions and a start and end time.

To reduce scope specify an end time (UTC) which means you will only see activity before that time. Specify the end time in this form (UTC): "23/01/2012 10:37:30 PM"

ExcludedOperations: To reduce scope you can specify operations to ignore by passing a list of operations to exclude. Pass operations to exclude in this form: Read, Write

Enables the resource activity tracking.
Resource activity tracking is available for locally managed Windows servers, SharePoint farms, and supported NetApp and EMC remotely managed hosts. It is used to collect data on identities, reads, writes, creates, deletes, renames and security changes on securable objects. This information is required for several report types, including the Resource Activity report.

The granularity for resource activity in minutes. This is the amount of time for the agent to collect and aggregate new activity before sending results to the server. Specify 5 minutes for testing/demo ONLY. Other valid times: 60 minutes (1 hour), 480 minutes (8 hours) or 1440 minutes (1 day)

A list of the managed paths that specifies where on a particular managed host and agent should scan.
A managed path is the root of an NTFS directory tree, or a point in your SharePoint farm hierarchy below which everything is scanned. The agent monitors the specified roots for changes to security settings.
For local managed hosts, by default the agent will do a full scan of the computer; however, you can optionally specify the managed path(s) to be scanned by the agent. Once you configure a managed path, only those roots are scanned.
For remote managed hosts, you must define the managed path(s) beofre scanning and real-time change watching can occur.
For SharePoint hosts, you must set managed path(s) before scanning can occur. When you choose a point in your SharePoint hierarchy as a managed path, new items below that point are automatically scanned.

Note: This must be present for remotely scanned managed hosts.
The schedule specifies the time and frequency with which the agent scans the target computer. This can be either day of the week or an interval or run once.
For day of the week, you must also specify the ScheduleDays and ScheduleTime parameter.
For an Interval, you must also supply the ScanInterval parameter.
For run once, you can specify the ScheduledTime; otherwise it scans immediately on agent managed path change.

This parameter must be specified for remotely scanned managed hosts that have the ScheduleType set as DaysOfWeek.
Supply the days you would like the agent to scan the managed host. The sytax is DayOne for Sunday, DayTwo for Monday etc. For example, to set a scan schedule for Monday, Wednesday and Friday, you would specify DayTwo, DayFour, DaySix.

This parameter must be specified for remotely scanned managed hosts that have the ScheduleType set as DaysOfWeek or RunOnce.
Supply the time of day the remote agent should scan on each of the days provided by the ScheduleDays parameter. For 4 in the morning you would supply 04:00:00, for 6 at night you supply 18:00:00.

This parameter must be specified for remotely scanned managed hosts that have the ScheduleType set as Interval.
Provide the interval on which the agent will scan the managed host in hours. For exampe, to scan every 4 hours you would supply 4.
